 Kilauea's eruption continues!
 Lava fountains reached about 660 feet, roughly the height of a 60-story building. It was episode 56 in an eruption that began just before Christmas in 2024, nearly two years ago.
 So why has it been erupting for so long?
 That’s a long run for a Kilauea summit eruption, considering some recent events only lasted a few weeks. Scientists think this one has settled into a kind of equilibrium: pressure builds in magma reservoirs beneath the summit, then lava fountains release it. 
 The cycle can repeat, and more episodes are possible.
 And Kilauea has had even longer eruptions. A separate eruption at Puu Oo, on the volcano’s East Rift Zone, lasted 35 years.
 So decades of activity are possible, though that was in a different part of the same volcano.
